input_signals.name: Operating Debt Capacity
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms producing operating profits large enough to support their debt burden should earn higher returns than firms whose financing obligations overwhelm operating strength.
input_signals.reasoning: The bounded ratio directly measures operating-profit capacity relative to total debt rather than relying on the known debt-issuance or deleveraging anomaly. Profitable low-burden firms receive positive values, heavily debt-burdened firms move toward zero, and operating losses remain negative, preserving directional consistency across the distribution.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( oiadp, add( abs( oiadp ), add( dltt, dlc ) ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Cash-Covered Total Payout
input_signals.expression: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(dvt, prstkc), at), 1), IND_ADJ(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(oancf, ADD(dvt, prstkc)), at), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Meaningful dividends and repurchases should predict higher returns when operating cash flow remains strong after funding those distributions.
input_signals.reasoning: Payout intensity is a nonnegative exposure multiplied by signed residual cash generation, so covered payers are positive, overextended payers are negative, and non-payers are economically neutral. Asset scaling avoids division by zero and broadening dividends to total payout improves stability and coverage.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( ratio( add( dvt, prstkc ), at ), 1 ), ind_adj( winsor( ratio( sub( oancf, add( dvt, prstkc ) ), at ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Accrual-Funded Equity Supply
input_signals.hypothesis: Equity issuance accompanied by profits that are not converting into operating cash flow should predict lower returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Issuance intensity is a nonnegative exposure to the signed gap between accounting income and cash generation. Thus accrual-heavy issuers occupy the high, unfavorable tail, cash-backed issuers can occupy the low tail, and non-issuers remain economically neutral rather than being classified solely by profitability.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( ratio( sstk, at ), 1 ), ind_adj( winsor( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Self-Funded Innovation Capacity
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 1)), IND_ADJ(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(oancf, ADD(sstk, dltis)), at), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: R&D-intensive firms whose operating cash generation exceeds external capital raising should outperform innovative firms dependent on equity or debt issuance.
input_signals.reasoning: R&D intensity identifies firms for which funding source is especially informative, while the signed cash-versus-financing balance distinguishes internally supported innovation from external funding dependence. Treating unreported R&D as zero is economically interpretable and preserves coverage without masking missing financing or cash-flow data.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( winsor( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), at ), 1 ) ), ind_adj( winsor( ratio( sub( oancf, add( sstk, dltis ) ), at ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Dilution-Adjusted Operating Improvement
input_signals.hypothesis: Operating-profitability improvement should predict higher returns only to the extent that it is not offset by growth in the outstanding share base.
input_signals.reasoning: The signal is scale-free because it uses asset-scaled operating profitability and share-count growth rather than changes in dollar profit per share. Dilution is penalized in proportion to the firm’s lagged operating-profit magnitude, while share contraction provides a corresponding boost, aligning both tails economically without relying on the standalone share-issuance anomaly.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_zscore( winsor( sub( delta( ratio( oiadp, at ), 1 ), mul( lag( abs( ratio( oiadp, at ) ), 1 ), growth( csho, 1 ) ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Profit-Backed Long Maturity
input_signals.hypothesis: Profitable debt-financed firms with a smaller fraction of debt due in the short term should outperform profitable firms facing concentrated refinancing needs.
input_signals.reasoning: The financing component is now the direct short-term share of total debt, so it isolates maturity composition rather than debt-to-assets leverage. Continuous profitability weighting concentrates both tails among firms with operating capacity while avoiding a profitability cutoff or a same-signed rank product.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( winsor( ratio( oiadp, at ), 1 ) ), neg( ind_adj( winsor( ratio( dlc, add( dlc, dltt ) ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Pre-Funded Payout Growth
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(LAG(RATIO(SUB(oancf, ADD(dvt, prstkc)), at), 1), 1)), IND_ADJ(WINSOR(DELTA(RATIO(ADD(dvt, prstkc), at), 1), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Increases in dividends and repurchases should predict higher returns when preceded by sufficient operating cash flow after existing payouts.
input_signals.reasoning: This repairs the failed payout-coverage change construction by measuring payout growth directly rather than embedding its negative inside the coverage change. Lagged residual cash capacity weights the financing decision, distinguishing pre-funded distribution increases from increases unsupported by prior cash generation.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( winsor( lag( ratio( sub( oancf, add( dvt, prstkc ) ), at ), 1 ), 1 ) ), ind_adj( winsor( delta( ratio( add( dvt, prstkc ), at ), 1 ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cash-Matched Buyback
input_signals.hypothesis: Buybacks that are meaningfully matched by positive operating cash generation should predict higher returns, while repurchases conducted amid negative operating cash flow should predict lower returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The bounded matching ratio is nonzero only when buybacks and operating cash flow are both economically meaningful, and it declines when either side overwhelms the other. This removes share-count growth entirely, avoids the standalone issuance anomaly, and limits scale skew without requiring a thin three-way product.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( sign( oancf ), ratio( min( abs( oancf ), abs( prstkc ) ), add( abs( oancf ), abs( prstkc ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cash-Strained Equity Recycling
input_signals.expression: MUL(RATIO(MIN(ABS(sstk), ABS(prstkc)), ADD(at, ADD(ABS(sstk), ABS(prstkc)))), NEG(IND_ADJ(WINSOR(RATIO(oancf, at), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms simultaneously issuing and repurchasing substantial equity while generating weak operating cash flow should earn lower subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The bounded financing term measures equity recycling—the overlapping portion of issuance and repurchases—rather than net issuance or issuance-related cash realization. Weak cash profitability gives this activity a positive adverse score, while cash-rich recyclers enter the favorable tail and firms without simultaneous flows remain neutral.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ratio( min( abs( sstk ), abs( prstkc ) ), add( at, add( abs( sstk ), abs( prstkc ) ) ) ), neg( ind_adj( winsor( ratio( oancf, at ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Maturity Funding Gap
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms whose short-term debt exceeds the combined support of operating cash generation and long-term refinancing should earn lower subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces repeated short-debt-share conditioning with a direct funding-gap measure: current maturities are compared with both internal cash capacity and completed long-term financing. Long-term issuance reduces risk only when it closes the maturity gap, so the signal captures refinancing sufficiency rather than generic low profitability or leverage.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( dlc, add( oancf, dltis ) ), at ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Distribution Funding Match
input_signals.expression: MUL(INDICATOR(SUB(ADD(dvt, prstkc), oancf), 0), WINSOR(RATIO(MIN(ABS(ADD(sstk, dltis)), ABS(SUB(ADD(dvt, prstkc), oancf))), ADD(at, ADD(ABS(ADD(sstk, dltis)), ABS(SUB(ADD(dvt, prstkc), oancf))))), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: External financing that closely matches a positive shareholder-distribution cash shortfall should predict lower subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The economically justified shortfall indicator prevents cash-rich capital raisers from being assigned mechanically to a favorable extreme, addressing a likely source of weak portfolio evidence in the earlier funding-gap signal. The bounded overlap term is large only when external capital and an actual payout shortfall are simultaneously meaningful.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( indicator( sub( add( dvt, prstkc ), oancf ), 0 ), winsor( ratio( min( abs( add( sstk, dltis ) ), abs( sub( add( dvt, prstkc ), oancf ) ) ), add( at, add( abs( add( sstk, dltis ) ), abs( sub( add( dvt, prstkc ), oancf ) ) ) ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Cash-Quality Repurchase
input_signals.hypothesis: Repurchases accompanied by cash-backed rather than accrual-heavy earnings should predict higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Repurchase intensity provides nonnegative exposure to signed earnings quality, so cash-generative repurchasers enter the favorable tail and accrual-heavy repurchasers enter the adverse tail. This tests whether the successful accrual-financing mechanism reverses economically when firms return equity capital instead of issuing it.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( ratio( prstkc, at ), 1 ), neg( ind_adj( winsor( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Fixed-Claim Cash Buffer
input_signals.expression: IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(oancf, ADD(xint, dvt)), ADD(ABS(oancf), ADD(ABS(xint), ABS(dvt)))), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms generating operating cash comfortably above interest and dividend commitments should earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This abandons the maturity-gap refinement and instead measures coverage of recurring fixed financing claims using comparable annual flows. The bounded ratio distinguishes cash-supported commitments from structural funding deficits without being dominated by current debt principal or firm scale.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( oancf, add( xint, dvt ) ), add( abs( oancf ), add( abs( xint ), abs( dvt ) ) ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Liability-Funded Gross-Profit Efficiency
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms whose gross profit per dollar of liabilities is increasing should earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Growth in gross profit relative to the liability base measures whether financing expansion is translating into operating capacity, rather than linearly adding profitability and liability-growth anomalies. The scale-free ratio preserves economic magnitude and penalizes liability growth only when gross profit fails to keep pace.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_zscore( winsor( growth( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), lt ), 1 ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Innovation Dilution-Adjusted Conversion
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(LAG(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 1), 1)), IND_ADJ(WINSOR(SUB(DELTA(RATIO(oiadp, at), 1), MUL(LAG(ABS(RATIO(oiadp, at)), 1), GROWTH(csho, 1))), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Prior R&D intensity should predict higher returns when subsequent operating-profitability improvement remains positive after accounting for shareholder dilution.
input_signals.reasoning: Innovation per-share conversion produced strong portfolio alpha but modest cross-sectional evidence, while dilution-adjusted operating improvement produced the opposite metric profile. This interaction tests commercialization through asset-scaled operating improvement net of dilution rather than another gross-profit-per-share variant.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( winsor( lag( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), at ), 1 ), 1 ) ), ind_adj( winsor( sub( delta( ratio( oiadp, at ), 1 ), mul( lag( abs( ratio( oiadp, at ) ), 1 ), growth( csho, 1 ) ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Persistent Fixed-Claim Headroom
input_signals.expression: IND_ZSCORE(TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(oancf, ADD(xint, dvt)), ADD(ABS(oancf), ADD(ABS(xint), ABS(dvt)))), 3))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms that consistently generate operating cash above interest and dividend commitments should earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The fixed-claim cash buffer produced strong joint evidence, but a current surplus could reflect a transitory cash-flow spike. The three-period minimum tests durable downside coverage rather than recombining the buffer with another issuance anomaly, while the bounded underlying ratio limits outlier sensitivity.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_zscore( ts_min( ratio( sub( oancf, add( xint, dvt ) ), add( abs( oancf ), add( abs( xint ), abs( dvt ) ) ) ), 3 ) )

input_signals.name: Self-Funded Organizational Capital
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(xsga, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at), 1), 3)), IND_ADJ(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(oancf, ADD(sstk, dltis)), at), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms persistently investing in non-R&D organizational capital should outperform when that investment is supported by operating cash rather than external issuance.
input_signals.reasoning: Non-R&D SG&A is treated as organizational-capital formation with a potentially positive return relation, directly addressing the ambiguous sign of the overhead interpretation. Persistent investment intensity weights a signed internal-versus-external funding balance, distinguishing self-funded capability building from capital-market dependence.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ma( winsor( ratio( sub( xsga, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), at ), 1 ), 3 ) ), ind_adj( winsor( ratio( sub( oancf, add( sstk, dltis ) ), at ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Innovation Financing Horizon
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms making persistent long-duration R&D investments should earn higher returns when their debt financing is correspondingly long-term rather than concentrated in current maturities.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces another commercialization blend with a financing-horizon mechanism: intangible investment creates value only when refinancing pressure does not force premature retrenchment. Lagged persistent R&D intensity weights the signed debt-maturity mix, distinguishing long-horizon funding from maturity mismatch.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( winsor( lag( ma( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), at ), 3 ), 1 ), 1 ) ), neg( ind_adj( winsor( ratio( dlc, add( dlc, dltt ) ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Fixed-Claim Innovation Crowding
input_signals.hypothesis: Large recurring interest and dividend claims combined with declining R&D intensity should predict lower subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This measures the crowding-out outcome directly rather than placing another R&D rank in front of the fixed-claim buffer. Fixed claims become adverse when innovation spending is being retrenched, while firms maintaining or expanding R&D despite those commitments enter the favorable tail.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( ratio( add( xint, dvt ), at ), 1 ), neg( ind_adj( winsor( trend( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), at ), 3 ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Depreciation-Backed Debt Issue
input_signals.hypothesis: Long-term debt issuance should predict higher returns when noncash depreciation capacity substantially exceeds interest expense.
input_signals.reasoning: This tests a distinct tangible-capital financing mechanism rather than another low-profitability debt-issuance interaction. Depreciation relative to interest proxies the internal recovery and tax-shield capacity available to support new debt, while issuers lacking that support enter the adverse tail.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( winsor( ratio( dltis, at ), 1 ), ind_adj( winsor( ratio( sub( dp, xint ), at ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Operating Funding Surplus Ratio
input_signals.expression: IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(oiadp, ADD(sstk, dltis)), ADD(at, ADD(ABS(oiadp), ABS(ADD(sstk, dltis))))), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms producing operating profit large enough to exceed external equity and debt raising should earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The signal embeds operating capacity and external funding demand in one stable, continuously scaled surplus rather than multiplying two archived legs. The asset-plus-flow denominator limits extreme values and preserves coverage while penalizing capital raising only relative to the operating profit available to support it.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( oiadp, add( sstk, dltis ) ), add( at, add( abs( oiadp ), abs( add( sstk, dltis ) ) ) ) ), 1 ) )
